$comment: ANTI-mirror map for backend/disclosure <-> frontend/lib/disclosure
(openspec: replace-observation-with-sightings, tasks.md 7.3 —
`disclosure` is Go-sole-authority, no TypeScript mirror now or ever;
add-proximity-disclosure's own Decision 1 is that designation, and
shipped cross-stack-determinism binds it to an anti-mirror check: 'A
mirror map for a capability designated Go-sole-authority (no TypeScript
mirror) SHALL instead run in anti-mirror mode: it SHALL fail if any
function name is declared in both the Go package and the designated
non-mirror TypeScript directory, unless that name appears in an
explicit, empty-by-default sharedNames allowlist recorded in the pair's
mirror-map file.'
Why this package in particular. backend/disclosure decides who sees
whom: its predicates are knife-edge float comparisons (passive range,
plume and sweep emission radius, star occlusion) whose outputs are a
player seeing or not seeing an enemy fleet. A second implementation of
any of them in JavaScript would not merely duplicate code — it would
produce a client that disagrees with the server about visibility at the
boundary, which is the exact failure this designation exists to make
impossible. The client renders the server's `contacts` array (the
system-interior read's top-level field); it never recomputes
membership in it.
This is the INVERSE of fixtures/market/mirror-map.json, the capability's
one remaining mirrored-pair map. That one asserts a mirror EXISTS and is
covered. This one asserts a mirror does NOT exist:
.claude/scripts/check-mirror-map.sh's anti_mirror pass over this map
fails if any function name is declared in BOTH backend/disclosure and
frontend/lib/disclosure unless it is listed in 'sharedNames'. There is
deliberately no 'pairs' array — a pairs entry would assert the very
mirror this designation forbids.
frontend/lib/disclosure does not exist and is not expected to, so the
anti_mirror check currently passes trivially on the 'TS_DIR does not
exist' branch (the same stated-trivial-pass shape 'space', 'system',
'fleet' and 'galaxy' take today). Should a frontend/lib/disclosure ever
be created for rule-bearing math (as opposed to wire types), that is
the moment this map's anti-mirror designation needs re-litigating, not
silently satisfied.
There is no fixtures/disclosure/cases.json: this package has no golden
fixture family of its own, so — like fixtures/fleet/mirror-map.json and
fixtures/galaxy/mirror-map.json — this file carries no 'coverage' or
'inventory' section. anti_mirror reads only 'sharedNames'.
'sharedNames' is empty BY DEFAULT and should stay that way. Adding a
name here is a claim that a render-side function may legitimately share
a name with an authoritative Go one; it needs the same scrutiny as a
spec change.
